#!/bin/bash
# =============================================================================
# devhost — run agent dev work on the BUILD HOST (node-2), not on the primary.
#
# Edit files on the primary as usual (your own git worktree — never /opt/nxeon),
# then run every heavy command through this helper. It mirrors your worktree's
# source to node-2 (/tank/nxeon-build/wt/<name>, own node_modules there), runs the
# command inside the capped nxeon-build-agents.slice with a THROWAWAY database
# (Postgres on node-2 127.0.0.1:5433), and streams the output back.
#
#   scripts/devhost run [--lock] [--max SEC] -- CMD...   push + run CMD in the node-2 copy
#   scripts/devhost tsc                                  = run -- npx tsc --noEmit
#   scripts/devhost test [FILES...]                      = run --lock -- npx tsx --test ...
#   scripts/devhost build                                = run --lock -- npx next build
#   scripts/devhost dev [--port P]                       start `next dev` on node-2 (background unit)
#   scripts/devhost bg NAME [--port P] -- CMD...         any background process (worker, preview server)
#   scripts/devhost stop [NAME|all]                      stop this worktree's background units
#   scripts/devhost logs [NAME] [-n N] [-f]              journal of a background unit (default: dev)
#   scripts/devhost tunnel PORT [LOCAL_PORT]             ssh -L so the primary can curl/Playwright it
#   scripts/devhost pull REMOTE_PATH [LOCAL_DEST]        copy results (screenshots, reports) back
#   scripts/devhost push                                 just sync files (run does this itself)
#   scripts/devhost install                              force npm install + prisma generate there
#   scripts/devhost db push|reset|info                   throwaway DB: schema push / recreate / name
#   scripts/devhost env set KEY=VALUE | unset KEY | list extra env for this worktree (never prod secrets)
#   scripts/devhost rm                                   stop units, drop the throwaway DB, delete the node-2 copy
#   scripts/devhost ls | status | sync                   workspaces / node-2 load / push refs to node-2's mirror
#
# Rules: /root/agent-notes/BUILD-HOST.md. The node-2 copy is a build/run sandbox,
# not a place to edit or commit — your primary-side worktree stays the source of truth.
# =============================================================================
set -euo pipefail
HERE="$(dirname "$(readlink -f "$0")")"
# shellcheck source=lib/buildhost-env.sh
source "$HERE/lib/buildhost-env.sh"
REPO="${DEVHOST_REPO:-/opt/nxeon}"

die() { echo "devhost: $*" >&2; exit 1; }
say() { echo "devhost: $*" >&2; }
q() { printf '%q ' "$@"; }

# ---- workspace identity -----------------------------------------------------
worktree_root() {
  local top; top=$(git rev-parse --show-toplevel 2>/dev/null) || die "run this inside your own git worktree of the Nxeon repo"
  top=$(readlink -f "$top")
  case "$top" in
    /opt/nxeon|/opt/nxeon-staging|/tank/nxeon-deploy/*) die "$top is a live/deploy tree. Create your own worktree first:  git -C /opt/nxeon worktree add /tank/dev-worktrees/<name> -b <branch> main" ;;
  esac
  [ -L "$top/.next" ] && die "$top/.next is a symlink (a live tree) — refusing"
  [ -L "$top/node_modules" ] && say "warning: $top/node_modules is a symlink — never 'git add -A' here (see BUILD-HOST.md). devhost does not need local node_modules at all."
  echo "$top"
}
ws_name() {
  local top="$1" n
  n=$(basename "$top" | tr 'A-Z' 'a-z' | tr -c 'a-z0-9-\n' '-' | sed -E 's/-+/-/g; s/^-//; s/-$//' | cut -c1-40)
  [ -n "$n" ] || n=wt
  echo "${DEVHOST_NAME:-$n}"
}
init_ws() {
  TOP=$(worktree_root); NAME=$(ws_name "$TOP")
  case "$NAME" in *[!a-z0-9-]*|"") die "bad workspace name '$NAME' (DEVHOST_NAME=...)";; esac

The minecraft adapter import looks client-safe since it's pure. Now I'm planning out the concrete file structure for lib/cyrus/modelstudio, starting with a math module providing vector and matrix utilities with a display transform helper.

Next I'm sketching the scene module's data model — triangle and UV buffers, part/face indexing, texture regions — plus a builder that converts a rig spec and skin layout into this scene representation by iterating each cuboid's faces, emitting two triangles per face with UV coordinates mapped from the texture layout rectangles, considering whether to export the existing face-corner helper from preview.ts for reuse.

For item sprites, I'm thinking through how to extrude a flat 16x16 texture into front and back quads at fixed depths with mirrored UVs, and weighing how painting should behave on transparent texels outside the item's silhouette versus how the renderer alpha-tests those pixels for display.

So both faces map to the same pixel, keeping texturing consistent front and back. Next I'm planning the glTF parsing layer: extracting scene geometry with world transforms, UVs, and texture references, plus helpers for bounding and camera-fit scaling, followed by the actual GLB/glTF JSON parser producing mesh data with positions, UVs, and indices.

I also need encoding utilities for test fixtures, validation guardrails against oversized or malicious input, and a picking module that computes nearest-hit intersections for raycasting against the scene, including mirroring hits across the symmetry plane for paired-part editing.

For performance, brute-force ray-triangle testing against 150k triangles per pointer move stays within a few milliseconds, well under the 16ms frame budget, so I'll skip building a BVH and just add bounding-sphere early-outs per part.

Next I'm defining the layer system: fixed channel types (albedo, normal, roughness, metallic, emissive, mask) and a Layer structure with opacity stored as an integer and standard blend modes.

I also need pixel storage per layer, encode/decode helpers using RLE base64, a channel compositor that blends layers deterministically with integer math, and since glTF textures can be non-square while my internal Raster type assumes square, I'll introduce my own rectangular Img type and convert between them.

Then for painting I'm sketching operation types for brush strokes, erasing, and region fills, where fill regions get resolved into pixel lists before application.

For determinism I'm storing fill masks as resolved rect/span lists rather than live scene references, plus decal stamps with optional clip spans, layer management ops (add, set, delete, move), and brush footprint rules distinguishing square versus round shapes, with symmetry handled by generating extra points in the same op.

I'm now designing `applyOp` and `replay` as pure functions that clone and mutate only the touched layer buffer, then sketching `session.ts` to manage an op log with undo/redo, periodic checkpoints, a step cap that folds older ops into the base state, and a hash function over the op log for verification.

For the hash I want something client-safe rather than relying on node:crypto, so I'm planning a small pure TypeScript sha256 implementation to drop into `hash.ts`. Then I'm defining the `ModelDoc` v1 schema in `doc.ts`, covering kind, base asset reference with its hash, texture dimensions, encoded layers, and an optional log summary.

I'm realizing the base reference needs to vary by type so saved docs remain reloadable: for creatures it should embed the actual RigSpecInput since it's small enough, for item3d it should include the full TextureDoc rather than just a key, and for mesh it can stay as just a geometry hash. I'm also sketching out `checkModelDoc` validation and caps like a max of 16 layers.

Now I'm defining `channels.ts`: the set of viewable render modes (lit, albedo, normal, roughness, metallic, ao, emissive, mask, uv checker, wireframe), with helper functions to determine which modes are enabled per profile and why — noting AO is disabled in Layer 1 since it's only baked at export time in later layers, not painted directly. I'm also adding a deterministic UV checker image generator.

For `contexts.ts`, I'm defining the VIEW_CONTEXTS (studio, gui, ground, firstperson, thirdperson, fixed, head, on_shelf) pulled from itemmodel preview contexts plus a custom on_shelf context, with transform logic mapping each context to a display transform — treating on_shelf as identity since vanilla items leave it undefined, though I'm flagging that assumption as unverified for the actual shelf renderer. I'm also building a matrix conversion function verified against the transform application tests, and a context placement function that computes camera and world placement for the three.js preview using hand position constants from held.ts.

Next I'm sketching `gripInHand` to validate that a grip point lands within tolerance of the vanilla tool's handle anchor point, returning a pass/warn/fail status with distance, and noting that creature entities only need studio and in-world contexts since they lack the item display contexts. Then I'm outlining the remaining modules: a budget module with performance constants and scene budget checks plus DPR capping for mobile, a merge module handling three-way layer merging with texel-level overlap detection and a "human wins" default resolution mode, and a service module wiring dependencies for the server layer.

Now I'm mapping out the model studio's remaining pieces: the draft store with model view/save/get/drop operations, HTTP handlers that gate access through a model studio flag check in addition to the usual viewer and rate-limit checks, the dependency wiring that ties together studio deps, the model flag, Prisma-backed draft storage, and preview renderer selection, and the access module defining the model studio flag constant and action-to-permission mapping. I'm also sketching the preview subsystem — a renderer interface with request/preset/cache-key types, a scene serializer that packages positions, UVs, and base64 texture data for the renderer page, a server-only Playwright-based renderer implementation, the actual HTML/JS page that runs inside headless Chromium loading three.js locally, and a PNG decoding utility I'm reusing from an existing library.

For the gate logic, I'm planning to extend asset-gate.ts with a model-specific permission function mapping actions like view/orbit/preview/export/install to ungated access while paint/fill/decal/layer/save/draft require edit permission, fail-closed and top-plan-only per the task requirements. I'm also weighing how adding "model" as a studio kind ripples through the plan matrix, studio name mapping, and the StudioLock component — since StudioLock's locked-state UI is currently texture/sound-specific, I'm leaning toward rendering a read-only ModelStudio view instead when access is locked.

Now I'm sketching the client-side structure: a ModelStudio page component with the three-column layout (model list/UV canvas/layers on the left, viewport and prompt dock in the center, in-game context and preview tabs on the right), plus a separate three.js viewport engine class handling scene setup, texture compositing, orbit controls, and raycasting.

For picking, I'll use three's Raycaster to generate the ray from the camera, then feed that origin/direction into our own pure triangle-picking logic so it stays testable. For code-splitting, I'm planning a client-only lazy wrapper around ModelStudio using next/dynamic with ssr disabled, so the three.js bundle only loads on the studio route.

For the in-game preview pane, I'm leaning toward a second three.js renderer that applies the displayMatrix from contexts.ts to the model, since flat 2D canvas rendering won't handle 3D cuboid/mesh transforms correctly — running two WebGL contexts should be fine on budget.

Rather than full scene authoring with a player arm, I'll simplify: reuse the same engine class in a "context" mode showing the model transformed plus minimal props like a hand box for first/third-person context and a slot square for GUI context, each with its own camera.

I also need the gun-in-hand math to stay correct: the display transform must position the model relative to the hand anchor, and the first/third person camera setups need to match exactly what held.ts does, so I'll port those constants and basis functions over rather than re-deriving them.

Wiring that override into the sync/deliver pipeline is outside scope here, so I should flag it for the owner rather than quietly skip it. The bow is held at its center rather than at a handle offset, unlike other tools, so its grip point should be defined differently — more like the sprite's middle. Vanilla's bow thirdperson transform uses rotation [-80,260,-40], translation [-1,-2,2.5], and scale 0.9, which confirms the grip reference is near the bow's visual center.

For categorization, I'm sorting into tool/sword/wand (TOOL_HANDLE grip), gun (handgun grip point), and bow/crossbow (vanilla-verified placement, treated as a pass since the hand position matches whatever vanilla already defines). Since bow, crossbow, sword, tool, flat, and shield all default to vanilla transforms, the real check is whether overrides cause drift from that vanilla baseline — but the gun is Cyrus-invented, so its reference anchor is the handheld fist position, and comparing against that reveals the gun default misses by about 3.1 units in first person and 1.9 in third person, which fails my tolerance.

That first-person number is tricky though — vanilla doesn't actually render the arm when holding an item in first person (only the item itself floats, except for maps), so the "fist position" there is really just where the item should visually sit, making a first-person mismatch more cosmetic. Third person does draw the arm, so the 1.9 unit grip deviation there is a more meaningful warning. I'm leaning toward treating first-person grip failures as warnings rather than hard fails, though the mockup actually shows an arm holding the gun in first person, so I need to reconcile that against what held.ts actually draws.

So I'm settling on: third person is the real grip check with a fail threshold around 3 units, while first person is advisory-only since no arm is rendered there in vanilla. Running the gun through this, third-person deviation of 1.948 warns, first-person 3.1 and aiming 5.08 both warn as advisory rather than fail.

This also surfaces a real finding worth reporting: the handgun's re-grip is computed under the gun's own rotation, so in third person it lands about 2 units off from where a vanilla fist would sit. A proper fix would recompute the grip relative to the vanilla hand anchor so the distance resolves to exactly zero, though that logic lives in shared display code used by both the pack builder and Texture Studio, so changing it risks breaking existing packs and tests.

I'd rather not silently alter shipped defaults — better to report the numbers, surface a warning in the studio's checks, note a proposal in OWNER-ACTIONS, and spawn a follow-up task for the display.ts fix rather than doing it now. For regular tools, swords, wands, shields, and flat items I'll use TOOL_HANDLE; guns get the handgun grip point; bows and crossbows need special handling since vanilla holds them at their center — I want to compute the anchor from applying the category's default display transform with its grip, so bows with no overrides measure to zero drift while actual overrides show up as distance. For guns the anchor is just the handheld-tool hand anchor. I'm restructuring the comparison logic now...

I'm defining a gripReference function that returns the grip point, per-view anchors, and basis label for each category — guns use the handgun grip against the vanilla handheld anchor, bows/crossbows use a center grip against the vanilla bow display, and everything else falls back to TOOL_HANDLE against the category's default view. Setting up WebGL renderer and geometry...

Since roughness and metallic maps need grayscale data where all channels match, I need to convert single-channel values into RGB-equal gray images before passing them to the renderer, applying this conversion wherever preview requests build roughness or metallic maps.

For the camera setup, I'm handling two projection modes: perspective cameras computed from eye position and target lookAt, and orthographic cameras fitted to the transformed geometry's bounding sphere. When no explicit camera request exists, I fall back to a preset view using the bounding sphere's center and radius to compute a perspective distance that keeps the object framed.

For lighting, I'm mirroring LOOK.studio's setup with ambient plus three directional lights positioned along fixed directions targeting the origin, since directional light behavior only depends on direction, not absolute position. After rendering once, I extract the canvas as a base64 PNG, then dispose the renderer and force context loss to ensure clean teardown and deterministic output across SwiftShader runs.

I'm adding a few new icons (orbit, wire, uv, stamp, bulb) directly into the existing icon map file rather than creating a separate one, since conflict risk is low. Now I'm sketching out the client architecture, starting with the model API module defining endpoints for fetching models, saving, draft management, and preview URLs, then moving into the ModelViewport class which sets up a Three.js scene from buffer geometry and handles texture maps like albedo, normal, roughness, and metallic.

Still writing viewport methods...

I'm simplifying by keeping orbit camera state as yaw/pitch/distance/target, updating the three.js camera position each frame, and making sure the raycasting math matches the same fov, aspect, and lookAt setup as the actual rendered camera so picks line up correctly.

For near-vertical pitch I'm clamping to ±89 degrees to avoid the degenerate case where lookAt with a fixed up vector breaks when looking straight down, and keeping context panel viewports separate, read-only instances using the rig's own camera and model matrix without picking support.

Now I'm sketching out the ModelStudio component's state shape: current view and model key, a per-model editing session bundling the session data, base albedo image, scene, dirty flag, draft state, and symmetry settings, plus tool state covering brush/erase/fill/decal/picker/orbit modes, color, size, shape, mirror, active layer, view mode, overlay toggles for wireframe/UV, and lighting.

For performance, I'm planning to maintain a mutable "live" composited LayerSet per session that gets updated directly during a stroke so the texture upload stays fast, then push the completed operation into the session's undo history once the stroke ends -- caching the live state per session in a map so undo/redo can just resync from the session's replayed state. For gathering strokes, pointerdown on the model triggers a hit test and starts collecting points for brush or erase operations as the pointer moves.

I'm also working out interpolation between pointer samples so fast movement doesn't skip texels, filling regions on click with a flood-fill hit test, and building a few simple procedural decal stamps like a star, ring, and chevron that get clipped to the hit region and placed in the current color.

Now I'm planning the layers panel (ordering, visibility toggles, opacity sliders, blend mode, add/delete, with a locked base layer row), a UV texture panel showing the composite plus face outlines and hover highlighting, and the picker tool for sampling colors from the composite albedo. I'm also sketching the in-game panel's context and state buttons for items.

For creatures, instead of the context panel I'll show an "In world" preview with camera presets (front/side/back) using BetterModel rendering, since contexts don't apply to them. On the right I'm planning tabs for Checks (budget and limit validations), Paint (brush/symmetry/lighting settings), and History (an undoable op log where clicking a step jumps to that index), plus a header with name, kind, stats, and undo controls.

Below that I'm adding a palette bar with derived swatches, brush size options, shape toggle, and color input, plus a prompt dock for "Ask Cyrus to edit this model" that's disabled with an honest note that model edits aren't available yet since no AI backend exists for that. For mobile under 760px, I'm planning a read-only orbit viewport, a diff summary of painted texels, an in-game context selector, a checks pass indicator, and Approve/Reject buttons where Approve saves the draft as a new revision.

Rejecting drops the draft, and if WebGL fails I'm falling back to a server-rendered preview PNG, with a message if the renderer itself is off. For locked plans I want tools disabled with a banner pointing to the upgrade page, while orbit/channel/context browsing stays available. Autosave debounces at 5s idle with a 30s max, and on load I'll check for an existing draft matching the base asset and automatically restore it with a timestamped banner and a discard option. For save conflicts (409), I'm planning to refetch and do a three-way merge between the session's starting base layers, the live in-progress layers, and the latest saved layers.

For theming, I'll reuse existing light/dark tokens alongside my own scoped classes in a model-studio stylesheet. I'm sketching out the page route and how StudioShell needs a new "model" studio kind, plus an optional prop so texture/sound pages can conditionally show the Model link based on a server-side visibility check.

I'll use a cube icon for the model crumb, and now I'm ready to start writing the actual UI code, beginning with icon additions.

I'm designing the ModelStudio component to wrap StudioShell with a model-specific configuration, and I need to extend StudioShell's kind union and add a showModel prop so the segmented switch can display the Model Studio link.

For the Body, I'm loading the model data through modelApi.models, then deciding between a NarrowView and full Editor based on a media query check for mobile widths. I'm defining the editor state shape to track the current scene, base texture, session, live and starting layer sets, dirty/draft status, and figuring out how to construct this state from a model entry for both creature and item types.

For creatures I'm building the scene from the rig spec and layout, and for items I'm building the scene from composite albedo and grip data, rebuilding it only when the alpha silhouette changes since that's cheap for items. I'm working through a tricky case: when a draft exists, its layers won't align with a replayable log from the server's start state, so I need a way to mark that log as "folded" (not replayable) during verification, and I'm introducing a startIsSaved flag to track this distinction.

For undo/redo and loading, I'm computing composites across all channels from the live and base images, then updating them incrementally during strokes via region compositing, keeping the composite as a mutable ref plus a version counter to trigger re-renders. For the viewport, albedo always gets mapped, while other channels only show up if they've actually been painted on and the profile permits it -- and since this deployment only targets Minecraft, the profile restricts painting to albedo and mask, disabling PBR channels entirely, which matches the mockup where only Lit/Albedo are enabled.

Since there's no glTF mesh in the actual project data yet, I'm considering adding a sample mesh model purely for development purposes, gated behind a non-production environment check so it never appears in the real product -- just to demonstrate the PBR channel view and prove the mesh rendering path works, even though it wouldn't be saveable since there's no underlying base row for it.

I'd generate this sample procedurally client-side: a simple box with per-face UV islands and a procedural wood-plank texture, giving something paintable to test the PBR channels against. For the toolset, I'm planning out the paint tools -- brush, erase, fill with face/color mode, color picker, decal, mirror toggle, and orbit controls.

Now I'm sketching the pointer-event logic: on paint start, skip if the tool is orbit or nothing was hit, otherwise branch by tool (picker samples color, fill computes a region and commits, decal places and commits, brush/erase begin a texel stroke with optional mirroring); on move, I interpolate between the last and current screen positions, sampling texels along the path so fast strokes still hit every pixel.

Painting is restricted to the active layer's channel, blocked with an explanation if that channel isn't paintable, and for non-albedo channels I treat the color picker's value as a grayscale intensity. I'm also planning hover tooltips showing part/face/UV coordinates, a UV panel highlight for the active face, and an autosave effect that debounces unsaved changes with a "Draft saved" / "Saving draft…" status indicator.

For saving, I'm assembling the document payload with encoded layers and optionally the operation log if it's small enough, then calling the save API; on a 409 conflict I reload the latest version, merge my local changes against the new remote base using a three-way merge, and reinitialize the session with the merged result as the new live state while marking it unsaved relative to the new base.

After a successful save, I show a toast and reload the view with a fresh editor seeded from the saved layers. For the right panel, I'm sketching out the Checks/Paint/History tabs, starting with a readiness card that reports save status and texture quality using the existing quality-check utilities, plus item summaries and budget rows.

For the left column, I'm planning the models list with creature/item thumbnails — leaning toward 2D raster previews for items and a simple icon for creatures to avoid spinning up too many WebGL contexts.

Then for the center, I'm sketching the viewport layout with the floating tool rail, channel bar, brush ring, and palette, plus a disabled prompt dock. On the right, I'm designing the in-game preview panel with context switches (gui, ground, first/third person, shelf) and a locked-state banner for when edit access isn't granted.

For the narrow/mobile view, I'm planning a header card with name and revision info, a read-only viewport that falls back to a server PNG, a "what changed" summary comparing draft vs saved texels and layers, an in-game context selector, and approve/reject revision buttons gated by draft existence and edit permissions.

Given this component is roughly 900 lines, I'm going to write it carefully now along with the accompanying CSS file, then move on to procedurally generating decal stamps like star and ring shapes.

Now I'm working out swatch generation—pulling distinct colors from item textures or creature skin palettes, capped at 12—and figuring out how context previews work per state, resolving each state's texture from the view model entries and building a scene for the in-game viewport from that texture.

Next I need to implement textureQuality, checking what fields the QualityReport type expects for its verdict and check list.

  dev|bg)
    if [ "$cmd" = dev ]; then bname=dev; else bname="${1:?usage: devhost bg NAME [--port P] -- CMD...}"; shift; fi
    case "$bname" in *[!a-z0-9-]*) die "bad name $bname" ;; esac
    init_ws; port="$PORT"
    while [ $# -gt 0 ]; do
      case "$1" in --port) port="$2"; shift 2 ;; --) shift; break ;; *) break ;; esac
    done
    if [ "$cmd" = dev ]; then set -- npx next dev -H 127.0.0.1 -p "$port"; fi
    [ $# -gt 0 ] || die "no command"
    ensure_remote; push_files; deps 0
    unit="nxeon-dev-$NAME-$bname"
    bh_ssh "systemctl stop $(q "$unit") 2>/dev/null; $(q "$BH_TOOL/bin/run-capped.sh" agents --bg --dir "$WS" --env "$ENVF" --unit "$unit" -- env PORT="$port" "$@")" </dev/null >/dev/null
    say "started $unit on node-2 (127.0.0.1:$port only). Logs: scripts/devhost logs $bname -f"
    say "reach it from the primary:  scripts/devhost tunnel $port   (then http://127.0.0.1:$port)"
    say "or test it ON node-2:        scripts/devhost run -- curl -s http://127.0.0.1:$port/"
    say "stop it when done:           scripts/devhost stop $bname" ;;

  stop)
    init_ws; which="${1:-all}"
    if [ "$which" = all ]; then
      bh_ssh "for u in \$(systemctl list-units --plain --no-legend 'nxeon-dev-$NAME-*' | awk '{print \$1}'); do systemctl stop \"\$u\"; echo \"stopped \$u\"; done" </dev/null
    else
      bh_ssh "systemctl stop $(q "nxeon-dev-$NAME-$which") && echo stopped nxeon-dev-$NAME-$which" </dev/null
    fi ;;

  logs)
    init_ws; which=dev; [ $# -gt 0 ] && [ "${1:0:1}" != - ] && { which="$1"; shift; }
    bh_ssh "journalctl --no-pager -o cat -u $(q "nxeon-dev-$NAME-$which") $(q "${@:--n100}")" ;;

  tunnel)
    rport="${1:?usage: devhost tunnel PORT [LOCAL_PORT]}"; lport="${2:-$rport}"
    say "forwarding primary 127.0.0.1:$lport -> node-2 127.0.0.1:$rport (Ctrl-C to close)"
    # shellcheck disable=SC2086
    exec ssh $BH_SSH_OPTS -N -o ExitOnForwardFailure=yes -L "127.0.0.1:$lport:127.0.0.1:$rport" "$BUILD_HOST" ;;

- worker: `CYRUS_SOUND_RENDER=ssh`, `CYRUS_SOUND_RELAY_PORT=<port>` (e.g. 7351), `CYRUS_SOUND_RELAY_TOKEN=<random, >= 24 chars>` (+ the existing optional `CYRUS_SOUND_RENDER_HOST/_ROOT`, `CYRUS_SOUND_LIBRARY_DIR`, `CYRUS_SOUND_FFMPEG_DIR`): the worker starts a loopback-only relay (`127.0.0.1`, bearer token, 4 MB request cap, one job at a time) in front of `sshRenderHost`.
- web: `CYRUS_SOUND_RENDER=relay`, `CYRUS_SOUND_RELAY_URL=http://127.0.0.1:<port>`, the same token. Build syncs and the Sound Studio's "Render and preview" / library audition go web -> worker -> node-2. The library-gated preview still needs `CYRUS_SOUND_LIBRARY_CLEARED=1`.
- health probe: `GET /health` on the relay (and `probeSshRenderHost`): ssh reachable, ffmpeg runs, library file count, work dir writable. No audio is rendered or stored on the primary (the relay forwards JSON only).

### 5. Admin visibility (`lib/cyrus/delivery/admin.ts`, `GET /api/admin/cyrus/ops?limit=`)

### Decisions made here (the plan did not specify)
- Test Flight results live on `ModBuild.cyrus.testFlight`, not on the revision: revisions are append-only (DB trigger forbids engine edits after creation) and many builds have no revision; a revision reaches its flight through `modBuildId`. No table was added.
- Deliveries are recorded on the GAME_MOD_SYNC job row (payload discriminator + `payload.result.cyrusDelivery`), not a new table; the on-server record + journal hold what a rollback needs.
- Health fails on NEW error lines (vs. the pre-change log) by default (`strictLog`); after a rollback only "came up" is judged (the previous state's own log is not ours to judge).
- A delivery restarts the server when the change needs it (`restartPolicy` "now" by default); worldgen and creatures can never be deferred.
- Data packs in mod deliveries are placed through the journaled fs (not the Mods engine placer); the on-server delivery record knows them. Mod Pack data packs are treated as restart content.
- Delivery of a part whose flag is off is a note, not a failure (same as R1); the master flag off refuses everything before the server is opened.

### Gates (all server side; the UI only shows the result)
- **Visibility** (`lib/cyrus/studios/access.ts studiosOpen`, `deps.ts studioViewer`): a Cyrus user (`modBuilderUser`: preview, or the public launch) AND (a preview account OR `cyrus_studios_enabled`). Anyone else gets the normal 404 page / API 404. Setting registered in `lib/settings.ts` and the admin settings catalog (default `false`).
- **Plan** (`studioPlanView` = engine-core `canAsset`): Texture Studio + Texture Library = the top plan `all` ("All models", it includes Yakko); Sound Studio + Sound Library = Saka and up; Free / Katara none. Only create/edit is gated: a mod's assets are always listed and viewable (locked pages show them read only). An unknown plan (lookup error) fails closed for editing, never for viewing. Every write handler re-runs the gate.

### Owner defaults for the open design questions (`STUDIO_DEFAULTS` in `lib/cyrus/studios/access.ts`)
| Question | Default now |
|---|---|
| Plan names | exactly the code's: Free, Katara, Saka, All models (Yakko is the top model) |

### Routes and files
- Pages: `app/dashboard/cyrus/[id]/studio/texture` (editor; plans that may not edit get the locked state in place), `.../studio/sound` (locked / included states only: the Sound Studio editor is the next slice), `.../studio/plans?studio=texture|sound` (locked / included / plan-unknown + plan matrix). `app/dashboard/cyrus/studio-shared.tsx` = gates + crumb data. `/dashboard/cyrus/<buildId>?tab=assets` opens the inspector on Assets.

Every handler: viewer -> per-user rate limit -> input validation -> plan gate (writes) -> service. Errors are JSON `{ error, code }`.
- Libraries: `lib/cyrus/studios/{paint,editor,access,held,marker}.ts` (pure, client-safe), `service.ts` (logic over injected deps), `http.ts` (handlers), `deps.ts` (the ONLY file reaching Nxeon seams: modBuilderUser + preview list, settings, tokens `tierOf`, rate limiter), `store-prisma.ts` (Cyrus tables via engine-core store + the ModBuild chain, read only), `candidates.ts` (real change-build backend), `uploads.ts`. `lib/cyrus/textures/display.ts` (item display transforms).

Hooked in: `PreviewPanel` (Assets tab only when the server opened the studios, real mods only), `CyrusApp`/`shared.tsx` (`studios` prop, `?tab=assets`), `lib/cyrus/store.ts` (`studios`, PanelTab `assets`). Also fixed: `CyrusApp` read `realBuilds` from the store snapshot taken before `setReal`, so `/dashboard/cyrus/<id>` deep links never selected the mod.
- No new tables, no migration.

### Paint-layer persistence (decision)
A studio texture is a **TextureDoc** (`lib/cyrus/studios/paint.ts`): the locked generated base (an ordinary DSL `TextureSpec`, still bounded by `MAX_OPS` 400) + an optional **sparse paint layer** `{ size, colors[<=256 "#rrggbb"], set: [pixel, colourIndex, ...] sorted, clear: [pixel, ...] }` (+ `tile` profile, `supersedes`, `decision`). Painting never becomes DSL ops, so the 400-op limit does not apply to strokes (a full 64x64 paint is valid; tested). The doc is stored with the asset (`CyrusProjectAsset`, mime `application/vnd.nxeon.texture-doc+json`, provenance `{ doc, quality, pngSha256, basedOn, packSha1 }`, sha256 = canonical JSON) and **composited everywhere pixels matter**: canvas, quality checks (`docQuality` = `tq-1` on the composite), PNG, and the pack (`buildPack` accepts docs as well as specs). Paint is opaque only; erase = clear to alpha 0. An uploaded PNG used in a project becomes an all-paint doc (`spec: null`).
- **Saving** = a new `CyrusRevision` (kind `asset`, status `passed`, `expectedHeadId` optimistic lock -> 409 `stale_head`) whose manifest is the head's with `assets/textures/<key>.json` replaced, plus a new asset row (content-addressed). Revisions and rows are never edited. A failing composite (quality `fail`) is refused (422). If the mod's pack carries no sounds, the pack is rebuilt from every current doc and published through the existing pack store (`selectPackStore`; off = "built, not hosted"); packs with sounds are rebuilt by the next build (said in the toast). **Not wired:** pushing a studio-saved pack to servers (delivery reads `ModBuild.result.assets`); the next build ships it.
- **Builds keep studio edits** (`lib/cyrus/assets/sync.ts` optional `studioDocFor`, wired in `sync-deps.ts`): when a build returns a texture spec that the current studio doc *supersedes* (the generated spec it was edited from, or a candidate the customer rejected / accepted), the doc (spec + paint) goes into the pack and the asset row (origin `edited`, `keptStudioEdit`). If the build changed that texture, the build's spec wins and the studio edit stays in history. Without the dep, sync is byte-identical to before (tested).

cd /tank/dev-worktrees/cyrus-r16 && cat >> docs/DOCUMENTATION.md <<'EOF'

## Cyrus Model Studio: viewport and paint

Branch `feature/cyrus-r16-viewport` (from `feature/cyrus-r2`, 2026-10-10). Layer 1 of the Model Studio plan (`/root/agent-notes/cyrus-designs/v3-model-studio/MODEL-STUDIO-PLAN.md`): a three.js viewport and paint-on-model for every model a project already holds. **Nothing is deployed and everything is flagged off.** The UI follows the v3 paint mockup (`viewport-paint.html`), which the owner has **not reviewed yet**. Screenshots: `/root/agent-notes/cyrus-designs/impl-shots/modelstudio-*.png`.

### Gates (server side; the UI only shows the result)
- **Visibility** (`lib/cyrus/modelstudio/access.ts modelStudioOpen`, `deps.ts modelStudioViewer`): the studios gate (a Cyrus user AND (preview account OR `cyrus_studios_enabled`)) AND (preview account OR the NEW setting **`cyrus_model_studio_enabled`**, default off, fails closed). Anyone else: 404 page / 404 API. The setting is read through the host seam (`getHost().settings`); it is not yet in the admin settings catalog (owner action).
- **Plan** (owner decision 2026-10-10: Model Studio sits in the top "All models" plan with Texture Studio / Texture Library). `lib/cyrus/engine-core/asset-gate.ts canModelStudio(plan, action)` maps every studio action onto the existing `canAsset(plan, "model", op)` (ASSET_MIN_PLAN.model = "all"): `view, orbit, preview` = keep, `install`, `export` are NEVER gated; `paint, fill, decal, layer, draft, save, ai_edit` = edit = top plan only. Unknown plan (lookup error, typo, future plan) fails closed for those and never for viewing; an unknown action is `bad_request`, never allowed. Lower plans open the same page in **view only** (orbit, channels, in-game contexts, previews) with the gate's reason and a link to the plans page. The Model Studio row is NOT added to the shared `PLAN_MATRIX` (it would leak a flagged-off product on the locked page); it is `MODEL_STUDIO_MATRIX_ROW`. `studioPlanView().edit.model` exists. Tests cover the whole plan x kind x op matrix plus every action x plan.

### What it paints (nothing invented)
| Model | Source | Geometry | Texture |
|---|---|---|---|
| creature | newest CyrusProjectAsset kind `model`, mime RigSpec (a build's creature) | RigSpec rest pose (`restMatrices` = creature preview's `poseMatrices`, tested equal), box-UV faces with the creature preview renderer's face corners | the compiler's skin (`layoutSkin` + `skinTextureSpec`, server side) |
| item3d | every item texture (block tiles excluded) + the mod's ItemModelSpec | extruded like vanilla item/generated (front, back, open edges per opaque texel) | the TextureDoc composite (spec + Texture Studio paint) |
| mesh | glTF 2.0 (`lib/cyrus/modelstudio/gltf.ts`, bounded reader: GLB or embedded data URIs, no external URIs, caps 32 MB / 150k tris) | node transforms applied, TEXCOORD_0 | base colour image |
ItemCuboidSpec (3D cuboid guns, plan F3) does not exist yet; the mockup's 9-element glock is therefore an extruded item here. No project holds glTF meshes yet (L3/L4); a dev-only sample crate (`?model=sample_crate`, never in production) exercises the PBR lane.

### Pure core (`lib/cyrus/modelstudio/`, GPU-free, unit-tested)
- `math.ts` ray/triangle (two-sided Moller-Trumbore), barycentrics, UV -> texel (top-left origin, clamp or REPEAT), orbit camera ray (= the three.js PerspectiveCamera).
- `scene.ts` one triangle soup per model + per-face UV regions; `pick.ts` nearest hit (coplanar ties: the lower triangle, i.e. the cube defined first), mirror-X by reflecting the RAY (cube nets are not mirrored in UV space), UV islands (fill region for meshes), triangle rasteriser.
- `layers.ts` per-channel lossless layers (albedo, normal, roughness, metallic, emissive, mask), opacity + blend (normal, multiply, screen, add, overlay), integer maths, region recomposite; storage `rle1` (varint runs + RGBA, base64; an empty 2048^2 layer is a few chars).
- `paint.ts` ops in texel space: brush (square/round, 1-64), erase, fill (resolved spans: whole face / same colour), decal stamp (clip to the face), layer add/set/delete/move. Deterministic; symmetry resolved at input. Session = base + op log + cursor; undo/redo replay from cached checkpoints; one stroke/fill/stamp/layer change = one step; > 200 steps fold into the base. `checkOp` validates untrusted logs.
- `doc.ts` ModelDoc v1 (`application/vnd.cyrus.modeldoc+json`): `{v, kind, name, base (rigspec+spec | texture | gltf, by asset id + sha), tex, layers, symmetry, log {ops, folded, sha256}}`; `startLayers` = what client and server both start a session from.
- `channels.ts` profile-aware view modes Lit/Albedo/Normal/Rough/Metal/AO/Emissive/Mask: channels the game's asset profile cannot ship are disabled with the reason (Minecraft Java: albedo only; mask is an authoring aid; AO is baked at export, never painted).
- `contexts.ts` display contexts studio/gui/ground/first person/third person/fixed/head/on_shelf from `itemmodel` `stateDisplays` (the pack's own numbers; `displayMatrix(t)` is tested equal to `applyDisplay` on every vanilla category and the gun). on_shelf: Cyrus and vanilla items write no transform, so identity (unverified). **grip_in_hand**: the fist is FIXED at the point where vanilla tools put their handle (`HAND_ANCHOR` = item/handheld applied to `TOOL_HANDLE`); the in-game preview draws the hand THERE, not on the item's grip (the old preview drew the fist on the grip, so a gun always looked held). Per category reference: gun = vanilla tool fist; bow/crossbow = vanilla's own hold of the sprite centre; others = their vanilla handle. Third person is the real check (pass <= 1.5/16 block, fail > 3/16); first person is advisory (vanilla draws no arm while an item is held).
- `merge.ts` the conflict rule: 3-way per layer id and per texel; disjoint changes merge, overlaps are counted, the human wins by default; "Apply part" = selected layers only; deleted-vs-changed is an overlap.
- `budget.ts` the plan's numbers (60 fps <= 64 cubes, 150k tris, 4 x 2048^2 channels, 512 MB GPU, stroke-to-pixel 16 ms, phones < 760 px with DPR <= 1.5).

### Finding: the Cyrus handgun defaults miss the vanilla fist
Measured with grip_in_hand on today's defaults (`lib/cyrus/textures/display.ts displayFor`, used by the pack): the idle pistol's grip lands **1.948/16 block** from the fist in third person (warn) and 3.148/16 in first person (advisory); the template's aiming state 5.079/16 in first person. Cause: the re-grip is computed under the GUN rotation (`regrip(R(gun), g, TOOL_HANDLE)` makes the grip land where a tool handle would land under the gun's rotation), not at the vanilla fist. Not changed here (it changes shipped packs and is unverified in a client either way); a test pins the numbers. Owner action below.

### Client (`components/cyrus/studios/`)
- `ModelStudio.tsx` page body (models list, UV texture, layers; header with undo/redo, draft state, Save revision; viewport with tool rail B/E/G/I/D, mirror X, orbit O, Wire/UV overlays, camera presets, channel bar; palette + brush strip; prompt dock shown disabled: model candidates are not built; In game panel with contexts, states and grip status; Checks / Paint / History tabs). Phones: read-only orbit + What changed + Approve (saves the autosaved draft as a revision) / Reject (drops it). WebGL missing: the server preview PNG.
- `model-viewport.ts` three.js (MIT, `three@0.186`, dynamic `import("three")` so the chunk loads on this route only): on-demand rendering, DPR cap, nearest filtering for the pixel profile, DataTextures per channel, lighting presets (`look.ts`, shared with the server page), context rigs with props (glove + sleeve, slot, frame, shadow, head, shelf). Picking never uses three.js: the pure pick on the same arrays.
- Painting writes the live layers immediately (region recomposite + texture upload), pushes one op per stroke; items rebuild their extruded mesh when the silhouette changes.
- Autosave: 5 s idle, at most 30 s, to the draft; reopening restores it ("Restored your autosaved draft", Discard).
- Save conflict (409 stale_head): fetch the newer version, 3-way merge with the human winning, show the overlap count, save again.
- Entry: `/dashboard/cyrus/<buildId>/studio/model?model=<key>`; the studio switch shows "Model" in Texture/Sound only when Model Studio is visible (`showModel`). Not linked from the Assets tab yet.

### Save path (`lib/cyrus/modelstudio/service.ts`, `http.ts`, `/api/cyrus/models/v1`)
- `GET projects?root=` models + access + renderer; `POST projects/:p/models/:key/revisions {doc, baseAssetId, expectedHeadId, log?}`; `GET|PUT|DELETE .../draft`; `GET .../preview?preset=&size=&source=saved|draft&context=&state=` (PNG). Viewer -> rate limit -> validation -> gate -> service; body cap 9 MB.
- creature: a NEW revision kind `asset` (manifest = head + `assets/models/<key>.modeldoc.json`) + a ModelDoc row (kind `model`, origin `edited`, provenance `{generator: "cyrus-model-studio", doc, basedOn, rigAssetId, logVerified, delivered: false}`). **Compiling the paint into the delivered BetterModel skin is not built** (the save says so).
- item3d: the albedo composite becomes the item's TextureDoc (spec untouched, every differing texel = paint, half-transparent texels snapped for cutout with a warning) and goes through the Texture Studio's own `saveTexture` (quality bar, pack rebuild, revision), so it ships exactly like a Texture Studio edit; the layers ride in `provenance.modelStudio` and reopen when the pixels still match.
- Stale rules: item base row must be the current texture row; creature base must be the current RigSpec row and the current paint row; `expectedHeadId` -> 409.
- Op log: when the session started from the saved layers and nothing was folded, the server re-plays the log (<= 2000 ops) and refuses a save whose pixels differ (400 `log_mismatch`); otherwise `logVerified: null`.
- Drafts: NEW table **`CyrusModelDraft`** (projectId, ownerRef, assetKey, baseAssetId, baseHeadId, doc, timestamps; unique project+owner+key; no FKs). Missing table = 503 `drafts_unavailable`, never a 500. `CYRUS_MODEL_DRAFTS=memory` (non-production) keeps drafts in-process.

### Server preview render (`lib/cyrus/modelstudio/preview/`)
Injected `PreviewRenderer` interface + `previewRequest` (geometry and channel maps as base64, textures capped at 1024) + cache key `sha256(request + renderer id + version)` (in-memory LRU; the `CyrusPreviewRender` table is plan F1). Implementation `playwright.ts`: one fresh headless Chromium per render via `launchServer` (hard kill at the end, 60 s timeout, V8 heap 512 MB, one renderer process, no /dev/shm), three.js on SwiftShader, DPR 1, no antialias, no tone mapping, one frame; **no network**: every request is intercepted, only the page and `three.module.js` + `three.core.js` from node_modules are served, everything else aborted, DNS mapped to nothing. `select.ts`: off unless `CYRUS_MODEL_PREVIEW=local`, and refused when `NODE_ENV=production` (production web/worker run on the primary, which never runs Chromium); the node-2 job transport for production is not built. Creatures face north, so presets turn 180.

### Tests and runs
- RAN on node-2 (`devhost test`): `test/cyrus-modelstudio.test.ts` (math, display matrices vs applyDisplay, grip_in_hand incl. the gun numbers, creature golden: every visible texel centre of every banshee cube face picks exactly its skin texel (1154 exact, 1074 occluded, 4 on a plane two cubes share), item and glTF picks, hostile glTF, mirror, layers round trip and blend maths, ops/replay/undo/fold, merge, doc, channels, budget, sha256 vs node, the full gate matrix, service + HTTP with fakes). Stroke-to-pixel at 2048^2 (16 px round dab + region recomposite, CPU only, GPU upload not included): median under 1 ms.
- RAN on node-2: `test/cyrus-modelstudio-render.test.ts` with real Chromium + three.js on SwiftShader: 4 golden images (banshee three-quarter / back, pistol studio / third-person rig) in `test/fixtures/cyrus-modelstudio/`, ~0.4-1.3 s per render, the same input twice = 0 differing pixels, separate launches 0.000 % off. Regenerate: `UPDATE_MODELSTUDIO_GOLDEN=1` and look at every PNG.
- RAN: fixtures through the real Prisma store (`scripts/cyrus/studio-fixtures.ts` then `scripts/cyrus/modelstudio-fixtures.ts`: creature + item saves, both logs verified) and Playwright screenshots against `devhost dev` (`scripts/cyrus/modelstudio-shots.mjs`).
- NOT RUN: any real Minecraft client (display transforms, grip, painted creature skins); production DB / migration; the node-2 preview job transport; GPU-memory and real-GPU frame-rate measurement (headless SwiftShader only); AI model candidates (no backend).
EOF

Third person is the real check (pass <= 1.5/16 block, fail > 3/16); first person is advisory (vanilla draws no arm while an item is held).
- `merge.ts` the conflict rule: 3-way per layer id and per texel; disjoint changes merge, overlaps are counted, the human wins by default; "Apply part" = selected layers only; deleted-vs-changed is an overlap.
- `budget.ts` the plan's numbers (60 fps <= 64 cubes, 150k tris, 4 x 2048^2 channels, 512 MB GPU, stroke-to-pixel 16 ms, phones < 760 px with DPR <= 1.5).

### Finding: the Cyrus handgun defaults miss the vanilla fist
Measured with grip_in_hand on today's defaults (`lib/cyrus/textures/display.ts displayFor`, used by the pack): the idle pistol's grip lands **1.948/16 block** from the fist in third person (warn) and 3.148/16 in first person (advisory); the template's aiming state 5.079/16 in first person. Cause: the re-grip is computed under the GUN rotation (`regrip(R(gun), g, TOOL_HANDLE)` makes the grip land where a tool handle would land under the gun's rotation), not at the vanilla fist. Not changed here (it changes shipped packs and is unverified in a client either way); a test pins the numbers. Owner action below.

### Client (`components/cyrus/studios/`)
- `ModelStudio.tsx` page body (models list, UV texture, layers; header with undo/redo, draft state, Save revision; viewport with tool rail B/E/G/I/D, mirror X, orbit O, Wire/UV overlays, camera presets, channel bar; palette + brush strip; prompt dock shown disabled: model candidates are not built; In game panel with contexts, states and grip status; Checks / Paint / History tabs). Phones: read-only orbit + What changed + Approve (saves the autosaved draft as a revision) / Reject (drops it). WebGL missing: the server preview PNG.
- `model-viewport.ts` three.js (MIT, `three@0.186`, dynamic `import("three")` so the chunk loads on this route only): on-demand rendering, DPR cap, nearest filtering for the pixel profile, DataTextures per channel, lighting presets (`look.ts`, shared with the server page), context rigs with props (glove + sleeve, slot, frame, shadow, head, shelf). Picking never uses three.js: the pure pick on the same arrays.
- Painting writes the live layers immediately (region recomposite + texture upload), pushes one op per stroke; items rebuild their extruded mesh when the silhouette changes.
- Autosave: 5 s idle, at most 30 s, to the draft; reopening restores it ("Restored your autosaved draft", Discard).
- Save conflict (409 stale_head): fetch the newer version, 3-way merge with the human winning, show the overlap count, save again.
- Entry: `/dashboard/cyrus/<buildId>/studio/model?model=<key>`; the studio switch shows "Model" in Texture/Sound only when Model Studio is visible (`showModel`). Not linked from the Assets tab yet.

### Save path (`lib/cyrus/modelstudio/service.ts`, `http.ts`, `/api/cyrus/models/v1`)
- `GET projects?root=` models + access + renderer; `POST projects/:p/models/:key/revisions {doc, baseAssetId, expectedHeadId, log?}`; `GET|PUT|DELETE .../draft`; `GET .../preview?preset=&size=&source=saved|draft&context=&state=` (PNG). Viewer -> rate limit -> validation -> gate -> service; body cap 9 MB.
- creature: a NEW revision kind `asset` (manifest = head + `assets/models/<key>.modeldoc.json`) + a ModelDoc row (kind `model`, origin `edited`, provenance `{generator: "cyrus-model-studio", doc, basedOn, rigAssetId, logVerified, delivered: false}`). **Compiling the paint into the delivered BetterModel skin is not built** (the save says so).
- item3d: the albedo composite becomes the item's TextureDoc (spec untouched, every differing texel = paint, half-transparent texels snapped for cutout with a warning) and goes through the Texture Studio's own `saveTexture` (quality bar, pack rebuild, revision), so it ships exactly like a Texture Studio edit; the layers ride in `provenance.modelStudio` and reopen when the pixels still match.
- Stale rules: item base row must be the current texture row; creature base must be the current RigSpec row and the current paint row; `expectedHeadId` -> 409.
- Op log: when the session started from the saved layers and nothing was folded, the server re-plays the log (<= 2000 ops) and refuses a save whose pixels differ (400 `log_mismatch`); otherwise `logVerified: null`.
- Drafts: NEW table **`CyrusModelDraft`** (projectId, ownerRef, assetKey, baseAssetId, baseHeadId, doc, timestamps; unique project+owner+key; no FKs). Missing table = 503 `drafts_unavailable`, never a 500. `CYRUS_MODEL_DRAFTS=memory` (non-production) keeps drafts in-process.

### Server preview render (`lib/cyrus/modelstudio/preview/`)
Injected `PreviewRenderer` interface + `previewRequest` (geometry and channel maps as base64, textures capped at 1024) + cache key `sha256(request + renderer id + version)` (in-memory LRU; the `CyrusPreviewRender` table is plan F1). Implementation `playwright.ts`: one fresh headless Chromium per render via `launchServer` (hard kill at the end, 60 s timeout, V8 heap 512 MB, one renderer process, no /dev/shm), three.js on SwiftShader, DPR 1, no antialias, no tone mapping, one frame; **no network**: every request is intercepted, only the page and `three.module.js` + `three.core.js` from node_modules are served, everything else aborted, DNS mapped to nothing. `select.ts`: off unless `CYRUS_MODEL_PREVIEW=local`, and refused when `NODE_ENV=production` (production web/worker run on the primary, which never runs Chromium); the node-2 job transport for production is not built. Creatures face north, so presets turn 180.

- RAN on node-2 (`devhost test`): `test/cyrus-modelstudio.test.ts` (math, display matrices vs applyDisplay, grip_in_hand incl. the gun numbers, creature golden: every visible texel centre of every banshee cube face picks exactly its skin texel (1154 exact, 1074 occluded, 4 on a plane two cubes share), item and glTF picks, hostile glTF, mirror, layers round trip and blend maths, ops/replay/undo/fold, merge, doc, channels, budget, sha256 vs node, the full gate matrix, service + HTTP with fakes). - RAN on node-2: `test/cyrus-modelstudio-render.test.ts` with real Chromium + three.js on SwiftShader: 4 golden images (banshee three-quarter / back, pistol studio / third-person rig) in `test/fixtures/cyrus-modelstudio/`, ~0.4-1.3 s per render, the same input twice = 0 differing pixels, separate launches 0.000 % off. Regenerate: `UPDATE_MODELSTUDIO_GOLDEN=1` and look at every PNG.
- RAN: fixtures through the real Prisma store (`scripts/cyrus/studio-fixtures.ts` then `scripts/cyrus/modelstudio-fixtures.ts`: creature + item saves, both logs verified) and Playwright screenshots against `devhost dev` (`scripts/cyrus/modelstudio-shots.mjs`).
- NOT RUN: any real Minecraft client (display transforms, grip, painted creature skins); production DB / migration; the node-2 preview job transport; GPU-memory and real-GPU frame-rate measurement (headless SwiftShader only); AI model candidates (no backend).

Beyond that, I'm checking the tabs: the texture quality warning for palette size looks fine, and the grip warning is correctly showing. Painting is working now—stroke registered, history updated, tooltip shows correct body coordinates, and the saved ring decal and stripe are visible on the chest. But the camera fit is off: the creature appears too large and its head gets clipped at the top, so I need to reconsider the bounding sphere fit calculation against the vertical field of view and aspect ratio.

I'm checking whether anything after setScene changes the camera distance—preset calls only adjust yaw/pitch, resize just updates aspect from canvas dimensions, so neither should be the culprit. The units are in Blockbench scale (16 per block), so the creature's bounding sphere radius and resulting distance should theoretically keep it in frame, meaning I need to recheck the actual fov math to find where the clipping comes from.

I'm checking whether preset() runs only on scene changes, and tracing whether a stray mouse drag during the stroke interaction might be triggering an orbit instead of a tap, which could be altering yaw/pitch rather than distance.

Then I'm double-checking the sphere-fit math against the camera's vertical FOV and canvas sizing, confirming the renderer's setSize call uses the correct bounding rect dimensions on resize.

Rather than keep debugging this edge case, I'll just make the fit calculation more conservative with a larger safety factor and base it on the bounding box instead of the sphere, then re-trigger the fit after the first resize observation fires.

A few smaller fixes to make: the pistol's orientation looks slightly off but acceptable for now, the context labels are truncated and need shortening, and the camera button bar is getting clipped so I should remove the margin and narrow the buttons. For first-person framing, I need to point the camera toward the item and hand center using a properly fitted field of view.

I'm computing the bounding box of the mesh plus props to find its center, placing the camera at origin looking toward that center, then setting the fov based on the bounding radius with some padding, clamped to a reasonable range.

I still need to design a playback clock and scene-time API for the pure core, plus a way for the viewport to apply per-part transform overrides—likely by splitting geometry into per-part Object3D groups rather than relying on a single mesh or vertex shader—and an overlay layer system that lets objects attach and animate driven by that clock.

I'm sketching the clock as a deterministic `PlaybackClock` class (play, pause, seek, loop, speed, tick-driven time rather than wall-clock, with subscriptions), and a `SceneTimeline`/pose-provider interface where pure functions merge per-part pose overrides at a given time, keeping any rig-specific sampling logic out of this layer since it depends on server-only code. On the viewport side, I'm planning to render each part as its own mesh sharing material so overrides can be applied per part independently.

Since picking relies on static scene positions, I realize overrides would desync picking during animation, so I need a pure `applyOverridesToScene` function that bakes overrides into transformed positions for accurate hit-testing, plus an overlay system driven by the clock and a `renderAt(t)` helper for single-frame renders like thumbnails. For server-side previews, I'm adding optional `time` and `overrides` fields to the request, with the page applying per-part transforms to positions before building geometry, while pose evaluation at time t happens on the node side and feeds into that request.

content.thinking: The third-person compile failed again, so I'll accept that and instead check the existing impl-shots for the third-person image content, noting the phone is locked in the new version.

Third person is now rendering as a tiny dot — this looks like a regression from the per-part refactor. The issue is likely in how the bounding box gets computed via setFromObject when matrixAutoUpdate is false on parts and the mesh matrix is driven by the rig; since this now operates on a group rather than a single Mesh, matrixWorld may not be updating correctly before the ortho camera calculation runs.

The fix is to explicitly call updateMatrixWorld(true) on the mesh (and props) before computing the bounding box in applyRigCamera, otherwise the box gets computed in untransformed model units, producing a huge sphere and making the item appear tiny.

input.message:
Model Studio Layer 1 is built on `feature/cyrus-r16-viewport` (worktree `/tank/dev-worktrees/cyrus-r16`, head 99ec22f675, latest r2 merged). It is behind `cyrus_studios_enabled` plus a new `cyrus_model_studio_enabled`, both off. Not deployed.

**Ran on node-2:** tsc clean; full Cyrus suite 1755/1755. Real Chromium + three.js renders match 4 golden images (0 px drift between launches, ~1 s each, no network). 11 `modelstudio-*.png` shots (desktop dark/light, phone) are in `impl-shots/` and I looked at each.

**Built:**
- **Paint:** pure core in `lib/cyrus/modelstudio` (pick to texel exact on every visible creature texel, tools, undo/redo, merge). Lazy three.js viewport.
- **Save:** creature paint is saved as revisions; item paint goes through Texture Studio's save, so it ships.
- **Plan gate:** All models only, fails closed; viewing never gated.
- **Autosave:** new table `CyrusModelDraft`.

**Finding:** today's handgun defaults hold the grip about 2/16 block off the hand in third person. I didn't change it (it changes shipped packs); fix proposed as a task.

**Not run or built:** real client, production DB, production preview transport, compiling creature paint into the delivered skin, AI edits. The UI follows the v3 mockups, which the owner hasn't reviewed.

**Animation hooks:** `clock.ts` (play/pause/scrub/loop/speed), `pose.ts` (per-node overrides, posed pick), viewport overlays and `renderAt(t)`, preview `time`/`overrides`. Minecraft display logic moved to `modelstudio/minecraft/`.

Docs section and OWNER-ACTIONS entry added.
